chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—reported to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Muskan, who said:

Abu Basir narrated to me, saying: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a junub entering the well and performing ghusl in it. He said: “Seven buckets are to be drawn from it.” And I asked him about excrement falling into the well, so he said: “Ten buckets are to be drawn from it; but if it has dissolved, then forty or fifty buckets.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرَ: the well whose water is being discussed for taharah rulings
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state requiring ghusl due to major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: fecal impurity falling into the well
key_terms.ذَابَتْ: dissolved or disintegrated into the water, increasing the required drainage
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets, the prescribed amount to remove in one case
key_terms.عَشْرُ دِلَاءٍ: ten buckets, the prescribed amount in another case
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is to be drawn out from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on purifying a well if a junub bathes in it or impurity falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings regarding purifying well water after contamination. It specifies the number of buckets to be drawn when a junub bathes in the well and when excrement falls into it, with a greater amount required if the impurity dissolves in the water.
